extraction.name: Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning
extraction.description: Geometry problem solving has attracted much attention in the NLP community recently. The task is challenging as it requires abstract problem understanding and symbolic reasoning with axiomatic knowledge. However, current datasets are either small in scale or not publicly available. Thus, we construct a new large-scale benchmark, Geometry3K, consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language. We further propose a novel geometry solving approach with formal language and symbolic reasoning, called Interpretable Geometry Problem Solver (Inter-GPS).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem data is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 from two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The Geometry3K dataset consists of 3,002 problems and is divided into the train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem, including its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem data was further annotated with unified structural descriptions in formal language, corresponding problem goal, and geometry shapes. The formal language defines 91 predicates and their corresponding literal templates.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One set of formal language descriptions, problem goal, and geometry shapes per problem.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees. For human performance evaluation, annotators had a high school or higher degree, and human experts were graduates majoring in science or engineering.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work in this paper may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of geometry problem-solving algorithms and problem parsers.
